citation: Stack Overflow, Developer Survey 2025 (AI section), https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai ; Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2026 (sixteenth edition), https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026 and https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai . Accessed 2026-10-15.
source_tier: Company research (annual self-report survey run by Stack Overflow)
access_status: Fully read via page-to-markdown fetch of 2025/ai, 2025 landing, 2026 landing and 2026/ai pages. Methodology pages and raw data not opened. [uncertain] because fetch summaries were produced by a summarising model, not read raw.
sponsor_and_incentive: Run by Stack Overflow (owned by Prosus), which sells AI-related products and data licensing and has an interest in framing developer trust and the continued need for human knowledge. Data licensed ODbL 1.0.
exact_quotes: 2025/ai: "More developers actively distrust the accuracy of AI tools (46%) than trust it (33%)." (summary line, AI page)
2025/ai: "Complex tasks carry too much risk to spend extra time proving out the efficacy of AI tools." (page's interpretation, not a respondent quote)
2025/ai: experienced developers show "a widespread need for human verification" (page's interpretation)
2025/ai frustration option: "AI solutions that are almost right, but not quite" (66%)
2025/ai frustration option: "Debugging AI-generated code is more time-consuming" (45.2%)
2025/ai help-seeking option: "When I don't trust AI's answers" (75.3%, 29,163 responses)
2025/ai question: "How much do you trust the accuracy of the output from AI tools..." (rest of wording truncated in fetch) [uncertain]
2026 landing: CEO Prashanth Chandrasekar: "With AI, every individual becomes almost a manager of agents." (podcast quote quoted on the page, not survey data)
date_and_recency: 2025 edition: field dates and publication date not stated on pages opened [uncertain]. 2026 edition exists (sixteenth annual); field dates and publication date not stated on pages opened [uncertain]. Today is 2026-10-15.
key_claims: 2025: more developers distrust AI output accuracy than trust it (46% vs 33%), and highly distrust (19.6%) outnumbers highly trust (3.1%) by about 6 to 1.
2025: positive sentiment toward AI tools fell to about 60% from 70%+ in 2023 and 2024.
2025: the top frustration is near-miss AI output (66%), and 45.2% say debugging AI-generated code takes longer.
2025: 87% of agent users (approx, combined strongly+somewhat agree) are concerned about agent accuracy; 81% about security and privacy.
2026: trust is described as conditional: 48% trust AI when they can easily validate answers; 16% for low-risk or non-important tasks.
2026: about 93% rate citing sources as important for verifying AI answers; 72% go first to coworkers for work questions.
headline_figures: 2025 trust in accuracy of AI output, all respondents (n=33,244): highly trust 3.1%, somewhat trust 29.6%, somewhat distrust 26.1%, highly distrust 19.6%. Combined: trust ~33%, distrust ~46% (rounded sums 32.7 and 45.7).
2025 professional developers: highly trust 2.7%, somewhat trust 29.6%, somewhat distrust 26.3%, highly distrust 19.7%.
2025 learning to code: highly trust 6.1%, somewhat 31.3%, somewhat distrust 24.2%, highly distrust 19.7%.
2025 experienced developers: highly trust 2.5%, somewhat 28.6%, somewhat distrust 26.7%, highly distrust 20.7%.
2025 sentiment toward AI tools: very favourable 22.9%, favourable 36.8% (~60%); unfavourable 10.8%, very unfavourable 9.6% (20.4%).
2025 frustrations (n=31,476): almost right but not quite 66%; debugging AI code more time-consuming 45.2%; less confident in own problem-solving 20%.
2025 would still ask a person: 75.3% 'When I don't trust AI's answers' (n=29,163).
2025 AI agents use (n=31,877): daily 14.1%, weekly 9%, monthly or infrequently 7.8%, plan to 17.4%, copilot/autocomplete only 13.8%, don't plan to 37.9%.

2025 agent attitudes: accuracy concern 57.1% strongly + 29.8% somewhat agree; security/privacy concern 56.1% strongly + 25.3% somewhat; productivity ~69% agree; team collaboration ~17% agree. Exact statement wording not captured [uncertain].
2026: 48% trust AI when they can easily validate answers; 16% extend trust to most tasks that are not important work decisions (2026/ai page, no n given).
2026 landing: >87% trust AI output 'to some degree', up from 31% last year (conflicts in kind with 2025's 33% trust; likely a different question or framing) [uncertain].
2026 landing: ~7% trust AI for many tasks including important decisions; ~12% don't trust it for most work tasks [uncertain: fetch summary].

2026: ~93% rate citing sources important for verifying AI answers; 69.9% use AI agents to find answers to problems vs 43.7% maintained repositories and 28.8% trusted people (as worded on landing page).
2026/ai: 73% use coding assistants and agents daily; 66% dominant use case; Claude Code 66%, GitHub Copilot 59% among coding agents; 62% favourable at work.
sample_unit_and_population: Self-selected developers worldwide responding to an online survey run by Stack Overflow. 2025: 'over 49,000+ responses' from 177 countries; per-question n for AI items 25,695 to 33,662. 2026: 30,903 responses from 169 countries, 103 questions; per-question n on AI page about 10,900 to 13,900. Mix of professionals, learners and others; not enterprise-sampled.
observed_vs_stated: Stated: all figures are self-reported attitudes and self-reported usage. No observed verification behaviour.
what_makes_trust_justified: 2026 survey frames trust as conditional on easy validation of the output (48%) and on low-risk tasks (16%); cites sources rated important by ~93%. 2025 shows people fall back to a human when they distrust AI (75.3%).
what_it_costs: 2025: 45.2% say debugging AI-generated code is more time-consuming; 66% near-miss output. The page says complex tasks carry too much risk to spend extra time proving out AI tools. No hours measured.
failure_mode_class: Wrong code (near-miss output), over-reliance (20% less confident in own problem-solving), security (agent privacy concern), accuracy of agents.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident source. Not applicable.
limitations_stated: Pages opened state no limitations; methodology page not opened. Respondents are self-selected Stack Overflow audience [uncertain: inferred, not stated].
counter_evidence: 2025 trust level (33%) vs 2026 landing claim of >87% trusting 'to some degree' suggests framing-dependent results. Stated distrust coexists with high usage (2025 ~84% use or plan to; 2026 73% daily). Self-report says nothing about whether people actually verify.
verification_status: 2025 trust, frustration, sentiment and agent figures: read on the 2025/ai page via fetch summary, not raw HTML or data download; treat as [uncertain] on exact wording. 2026 landing and 2026/ai figures: read via fetch summary; question wording not shown on 2026/ai page, so [uncertain]. Survey dates, methodology and total-sample statement for 2025 beyond 'over 49,000' not checked.
usable_claim: In Stack Overflow's 2025 survey, 46% of developers said they somewhat or highly distrust the accuracy of AI tool output and 33% trust it; 3.1% highly trust it. 66% named 'AI solutions that are almost right, but not quite' as a frustration. Self-reported attitudes only.
do_not_use: Do not say developers verify AI output at a given rate (no verification-behaviour question found). Do not use the 2026 '87% trust' or 'up from 31%' figures without reading the question wording. Do not use agent usage percentages as trust figures. Do not cite the 2026 survey dates or total n beyond 30,903 from the landing page.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against The Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays [uncertain].
